purpose: Separate the historical/subcultural 'Da Sektur' referent from the broader Timic Sektur concept and model how adversarial attention ecologies reproduce through archives, reaction, monetization and platform migration.

historical_subcultural_referent.label: Ethan Ralph / Da Sektur
historical_subcultural_referent.description: Archived Kiwi Farms front-page snapshots show a board/category titled 'Ethan Ralph / Da Sektur' with the description 'The #Killstream and the smoldering ruins of a once great Sektur.'
historical_subcultural_referent.caution: Archive captures establish the label's public use in that environment; they do not establish every claim made inside the forum.

timic_generalization.label: Sektur
timic_generalization.description: Project-canon generalization: a semi-bounded social territory where attention communities, adversarial archives, reaction creators, fans/anti-fans and recurring roles become self-reproducing.

central_distinction: Historical Da Sektur is an externally attested subcultural label. Timic Sektur is a broader analytical/mythic category inspired by and extending beyond that milieu. Do not treat them as identical objects.

roles.subject-cow: Attention-bearing subject. Structural role only; not a moral judgment.
roles.farmer: Actor who cultivates, archives, frames, investigates, provokes, summarizes or monetizes recurring attention.
roles.dog: Pursuit/reaction/boundary role that can defend, attack, monitor, expose or amplify and may transition into Farmer when reaction becomes durable production.
roles.archivist: Actor or system preserving content and lowering the cost of future commentary.
roles.spectator: Audience participant whose attention, donations, subscriptions or social status can sustain the ecology.
roles.platform: Infrastructure distributing, moderating, monetizing or deplatforming the ecology.
roles.counter_public: Competing community or archive that challenges the dominant framing and can itself become part of the attention loop.

archive_effect.mechanism: archive -> lower retrieval/production cost -> more commentary -> more audience -> stronger incentive to preserve and react
archive_effect.risk: Old allegations can be repeatedly presented without their original evidentiary context, producing an illusion of cumulative corroboration.
archive_effect.countermeasure: Every serious claim should retain source, date, response, adjudication and contradiction fields.

joshua_moon_rule.description: Where the project means Joshua Moon / Kiwi Farms operator, resolve the exact person/platform/legal-entity relationship through reliable records. Generic 'Josh' references remain unresolved until context identifies the person.
joshua_moon_rule.prohibition: Do not infer misconduct from forum ownership or from hostile community claims without direct sourcing.

timic_mapping.Milk: observable output/reward such as views, donations, status or content supply
timic_mapping.Mud: residual allegations, screenshots, legal/reputational conflict and archived dispute
timic_mapping.Sektur: social territory in which Farm roles become culturally legible and repeatable
timic_mapping.Swamp: larger platform, legal, economic, institutional and information infrastructure surrounding the ecology
timic_mapping.Garden: counter-system focused on truthful provenance, protection, exit, repair and life-building rather than indefinite harvesting

research_questions: When did the term 'Da Sektur' first appear and how did its meaning change across Killstream-adjacent communities?
Which infrastructure providers, platforms and payment systems materially shaped the migration of internet-bloodsports communities?
Which subjects became economically sustaining nodes for secondary creators, and how can this be measured without amplifying harassment?
How often do archive communities correct false material compared with preserving it?
Which institutional safeguards let a subject exit a durable adversarial-attention loop?
How does the Farm mechanism compare with celebrity gossip, political opposition research, paparazzi and tabloid ecosystems?
